h1: The 5 Best GooDee Projectors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 GooDee projectors scored on streaming platform, focus system, resolution claims and price, from a mini to a 4K flagship.
summary: The GooDee 4K Smart Projector with 5G WiFi 6 is the best of the five, adding TOF auto focus and HDR-oriented brightness claims to built-in streaming. The GOODEE Mini Projector with Google TV is the better pick for people who want a familiar interface and a stated native 1920x1080 resolution. The cheaper 4K model and the AI Smart Mini round out the middle, while the budget Mini with WiFi and Bluetooth is the entry point.
intro: Buying a GooDee projector is mostly a naming puzzle. The titles all say 4K, WiFi, Bluetooth and built-in apps, so the real differences hide in the details: which streaming platform runs inside, how focus is handled and whether the resolution claim is native or a supported input. Pay for the wrong one and you are watching a dim, soft picture with a menu that confuses the family.

We ranked these five by the evidence in each listing. We reviewed only GooDee models, left other brands out, and the Primea framework gave most credit to the stated focus system, the streaming interface, resolution claims and the price bucket. Where a listing only says 4K without a native resolution, we say so.

products.name: GooDee 4K Smart Projector with 5G WiFi 6 & Bluetooth
products.verdict: The fullest GooDee spec sheet, with WiFi 6, TOF auto focus and built-in streaming apps.
products.description:
This is GooDee's most complete listing: a smart projector with built-in streaming apps, 5G WiFi 6, Bluetooth, ultra-bright cinema and HDR visuals and TOF auto focus with a smart screen. TOF focus uses a distance sensor, so the picture sharpens itself when you move the projector instead of making you turn a ring in the dark.

It leads because no other GooDee here documents both a modern wireless standard and a sensor-based focus system. It costs the most, in the $200 to $500 bucket, and the 4K label is a title claim, not a native-resolution spec.

Buy it for a living room that will see regular movie nights. Skip it if you want a stated native resolution.
products.idealFor: Households that want a sharp, no-fuss movie projector.
products.skipIf: You need a stated native resolution on paper.

products.name: GOODEE Mini Projector Built-in Apps
products.verdict: A mini projector with Google TV, voice control and a stated native 1920x1080 picture.
products.description:
This mini lists streaming with Google TV, the Google voice assistant and native 1920x1080 resolution. Google TV is the interface most people already know from a TV stick, so setup is a login, not a learning curve, and voice search saves typing with a remote.

It places second because the 4K flagship adds a sensor focus system and WiFi 6, while this one is the more honest on resolution, naming a true native figure. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket, half the cost of the leader.

It suits families who care about a simple interface and a documented 1080p picture. Skip it if you want auto focus detail, which the listing leaves unclear.
products.idealFor: Families who want a familiar interface and honest resolution.
products.skipIf: You want a sensor-based auto focus system.

products.name: GooDee 4K Smart Projector with 5G WiFi & Bluetooth
products.verdict: A 4K-titled smart projector that streams without an extra stick, for less than the WiFi 6 model.
products.description:
This is the older sibling of the flagship, a 4K-titled smart projector with 5G WiFi and Bluetooth that streams without an extra device. The listing also talks about ending the struggle of manual focus, which suggests an automatic system, though it does not name the technology.

It sits third because the WiFi 6 version names its sensor focus and HDR visuals, while this one leaves those details vague. It drops a full price bucket, $100 to $200, so it is the easy compromise.

Buy it to get the main experience for less money. Skip it if you want the wireless standard or focus system documented.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the 4K-titled model for less.
products.skipIf: You want WiFi 6 and a named focus sensor.

products.name: GooDee AI Smart Mini Projector with WiFi & Bluetooth
products.verdict: The YG600-Mini, a smart streaming mini with instant focus and AI optical technology.
products.description:
The AI Smart Mini is the YG600-Mini, running a smart streaming system with instant sharpening and what the listing calls advanced AI optical technology. Treat AI in a projector listing carefully: it usually means automatic correction of focus or keystone, which helps, but the listing does not say what is automated.

It lands fourth because the Google TV mini states a native resolution and the 4K models show more sensor detail. It is sized for portability at $100 to $200, level with the older 4K model.

Choose it if you want a small projector that sets itself up. Skip it if you want the resolution and brightness stated.
products.idealFor: Travellers and small rooms needing a self-setting projector.
products.skipIf: You need documented resolution and brightness.

products.name: GOODEE Mini Projector with WiFi and Bluetooth
products.verdict: The cheapest GooDee here, with built-in apps and a stable WiFi connection.
products.description:
The entry-level mini lists built-in apps, a stable WiFi connection and Bluetooth, and nothing about focus, resolution or brightness. Its job is to be the cheapest way into a GooDee, in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It finishes fifth because the listing gives you the least to check, and the Google TV mini costs only a bucket more while naming a native 1920x1080 picture. At this price, expect a smaller, dimmer picture best suited to a dark room, since the listing makes no brightness promise.

A fit for a bedroom wall or a child's room. Skip it for a living room or any room with daylight.
products.idealFor: Bedroom or kids' room movie nights in the dark.
products.skipIf: You watch in a bright room or want documented picture quality.

whatMatters.detail: Native resolution is the number of pixels the projector actually draws, while a 4K input just means it accepts a 4K signal. A 1920x1080 native projector is still sharp for movies. Look for the word native in the listing, as on the Google TV mini, and be wary of 4K in the title alone.

Auto focus saves you from turning a ring each time the projector moves. TOF sensors measure distance and adjust the lens, which is faster and more reliable than a camera-based method. Check the listing for the TOF label, as on the WiFi 6 model, and treat vague wording about instant sharpening as unproven.

Built-in apps remove the need for a stick. Google TV gives a familiar interface and voice search, while unnamed systems may have fewer apps or slower updates. Look for the platform name in the listing and check that the services you use, such as Netflix, are supported before buying.

WiFi 6 handles several devices and busy home networks better than older standards, and 5G bands cut the interference that causes buffering. Check the listing for WiFi 6 or 5G, as on the flagship and the 4K model, because a weak connection ruins a streaming projector.

Projectors lose contrast in daylight, so a bright room needs a brighter lamp than a dark one. Several of these listings give no brightness figure, which makes them dark-room products. Check the stated brightness on the product page, and plan on closing the curtains regardless.

faq.q: Do these GooDee projectors need an extra streaming stick?
faq.a: No. The GooDee 4K models, the Google TV mini and the entry-level mini all list built-in apps. Check that your services, such as Netflix, are supported on the product page, because some platforms limit app availability.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with a GooDee 4K projector?
faq.a: Assuming 4K in the title means a native 4K picture. The listings for the GooDee 4K models do not give a native figure, while the Google TV mini states native 1920x1080. Check the specifications before paying for 4K.

faq.q: Is the WiFi 6 flagship worth it over the cheaper 4K model?
faq.a: For a main room, yes. The GooDee 4K Smart Projector with 5G WiFi 6 names TOF auto focus and HDR visuals, while the cheaper 5G WiFi model leaves those details vague. For casual use, the cheaper one is enough.

faq.q: How do I set up a GooDee projector?
faq.a: Place it on a steady surface or tripod, aim it at a flat wall or screen, and let the focus settle. On the WiFi 6 model, TOF focus adjusts when you move it. Then connect to WiFi and sign in to your apps.

faq.q: How do I maintain a projector?
faq.a: Clean the lens with a microfibre cloth, keep the vents clear and let the fan run after you power off. Store the AI Smart Mini or any mini in a dust-free bag, since dust on the lens softens the picture.

faq.q: Can I use a GooDee projector in a bright room?
faq.a: Not well. Most listings give no brightness figure, and projectors wash out in daylight. The GooDee 4K with WiFi 6 pitches ultra-bright visuals, but close the curtains anyway. Entry-level minis are best kept for dark rooms.

finalTake: The GooDee 4K Smart Projector with 5G WiFi 6 is the best GooDee here because it documents TOF auto focus, a modern wireless standard and built-in streaming. The GOODEE Mini with Google TV is the smart alternative for a simple interface and a stated native 1080p. Treat 4K in any title as a label, not a measurement. Match the model to the room: a dark bedroom needs less than a main living room.
